title: handle_key(): Delete and Enter key handlers
description:
**What:** Add Delete (forward-delete) and Enter (trigger send flag) arms to handle_key() in event.rs.

**Algorithm:**
1. Delete arm (add after the Right key arm):
   - Pattern: KeyCode::Delete if state.focus == Focus::Input
   - If state.input_cursor < state.input.len():
     a. Start at state.input_cursor (already at a char boundary).
     b. Find end of current char: start end_cursor = state.input_cursor + 1; while end_cursor < input.len() && !input.is_char_boundary(end_cursor) { end_cursor += 1; }
     c. state.input.drain(state.input_cursor..end_cursor);
     d. Cursor stays at state.input_cursor (now points to next char or end).
   - If cursor == len, no-op.

2. Enter arm (add after Home/End arms):
   - Pattern: KeyCode::Enter if state.focus == Focus::Input
   - If !state.input.trim().is_empty() { state.should_send_message = true; }
   - If input is all whitespace: no-op (do not set flag).

**Defensive rules:**
- Delete must never move the cursor — only drain [cursor..end_of_char].
- After drain, state.input.is_char_boundary(state.input_cursor) must be true.
- Enter must NOT clear input here — clearing happens AFTER successful send in run().
- Enter must NOT directly call any async function — it only sets a flag.
- Use is_char_boundary, NOT a raw +1 increment for multi-byte chars.

**Agent team:** R reads existing Backspace and Left handlers as reference patterns; I implements both arms; T writes unit tests using handle_key() directly; V runs cargo test -p kith-tui.
